module.title: Unit 8: Complex Passive Structures & Impersonal Reporting in Journalistic Prose
module.objective: Mampu menguasai impersonal passive reporting (It is broadly asserted that, The phenomenon is believed to stem from).

subModules.title: Reading Mission: The City River Report

content.summary: Read a short report about pollution in a city river and the evidence gathered by local researchers. You will practise identifying the main point, finding supporting details, and understanding how journalists use impersonal passive structures to report claims without naming a source in every sentence.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Notice patterns such as It is widely acknowledged that the river needs attention, and The pollution is believed to stem from several sources. Use a perfect infinitive, as in The company is alleged to have released waste, when the reported action happened before the reporting.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Learn words for making claims, describing evidence, and explaining causes, including assert, allege, acknowledge, stem from, and corroborate.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Skim the opening and closing sentences to identify the report's main point. Then scan for names, dates, figures, and phrases that show what is known, alleged, or still uncertain.

learningObjectives: Identify the main idea of a short news-style report about river pollution.
Locate specific details about the investigation, its findings, and the proposed next steps.
Distinguish confirmed evidence from allegations and explanations that remain uncertain.
Recognize impersonal reporting patterns with that-clauses and infinitives.
Use reporting verbs to understand how a journalist presents a claim and its source.

contextWarmup.prompt: A local river has changed colour after heavy rain. What should a careful news report do first?
options: Check observations and test results before presenting a cause as fact.
Name a company as responsible before collecting any evidence.
Repeat the first explanation shared on social media.
contextWarmup.explanation: A report should separate what has been observed from what has been proved. Checking evidence helps readers understand what is known and what still needs investigation.

rules: Use It is or It was plus a past participle and that-clause to report a general claim: It is widely acknowledged that the river needs attention.

Use a subject followed by a reporting verb in the passive and a present infinitive when the reported situation is current or happens at the same time: The problem is believed to stem from several sources.
Use to have plus a past participle when the reported action happened before the reporting: The firm is alleged to have released waste last year.

Reporting verbs show how certain or well-supported a statement is. A claim that is alleged is not necessarily proved, while evidence that corroborates a finding supports it with additional information.

commonTrap.explanation: Do not use the present infinitive for an action that clearly happened earlier. The perfect infinitive marks the earlier time and helps the reader follow the report's timeline.
commonTrap.wrong: The company is alleged to release waste into the river last year.
commonTrap.correct: The company is alleged to have released waste into the river last year.

content.contractionsSubtitle: Contractions are common in conversation, but formal news reports usually use full forms:

contractions.subject: It
contractions.exampleFull: It is widely acknowledged that the river needs attention.
contractions.exampleContracted: It's widely acknowledged that the river needs attention.

contractions.subject: The findings
contractions.exampleFull: The findings are reported to support the earlier study.
contractions.exampleContracted: They're reported to support the earlier study.

grammarFormulas.title: Sentence Patterns with Impersonal Reporting Passives
grammarFormulas.description: Compare these patterns to see how a report can focus on a claim, a subject, or the timing of an action:

items.exampleSentence: It is broadly asserted that economic growth alone cannot solve poverty.
items.collocation: assert that a claim is true

items.exampleSentence: The company is alleged to have released waste into the river.
items.collocation: be alleged to have done something

items.exampleSentence: It is widely acknowledged that the river needs regular monitoring.
The change in water quality is believed to stem from several sources.
An impersonal sentence can report a claim without naming its source.
The latest tests corroborate the earlier findings.
The investigation found signs of contamination near the bridge.
Researchers will monitor water quality over the next six months.

content.passageTitle: What Is Changing the Water in Bellford River?
paragraphs: Residents in Bellford have reported a cloudy colour in the river after several weeks of heavy rain. It is widely acknowledged that the waterway has become more important as the town grows, but the reason for the change is not yet clear. A council report says that samples were collected at six points in March. Higher levels of sediment were found near the old bridge, while readings at two upstream sites remained within normal limits.

The change is believed to stem from a combination of soil run-off and work on nearby roads. A local group alleges that one construction firm has allowed waste to reach a drain, though the claim has not been confirmed. The company is reported to have denied breaking any rules. Researchers say that recent tests corroborate earlier evidence of sediment, but do not identify its exact source. The council has promised to publish new results next month and says the river will be monitored throughout the summer.

questions.question: What change have residents reported in the river?
options: Its water has looked cloudy after heavy rain.
Its water has become unusually warm.
Its level has remained low all year.
questions.answer: Its water has looked cloudy after heavy rain.
questions.explanation: The opening sentence says residents reported a cloudy colour after several weeks of heavy rain.

questions.question: How many places were sampled in March?
options: Two
Six
Twelve
questions.explanation: The council report says samples were collected at six points in March.

questions.question: Where were higher levels of sediment found?
options: Near the old bridge
At both upstream sites
Beside the town council office
questions.explanation: The report states that higher levels of sediment were found near the old bridge.

questions.question: What possible causes of the change are mentioned?
options: Soil run-off and work on nearby roads
A new water park and a dry summer
Farm waste and a damaged bridge
questions.answer: Soil run-off and work on nearby roads
questions.explanation: The change is believed to stem from a combination of soil run-off and nearby road work.

questions.question: What does the report say about the claim against a construction firm?
options: It has been confirmed by the council.
It has not been confirmed.
The firm has admitted responsibility.
questions.explanation: The passage says the local group's allegation has not been confirmed.

questions.question: What is the company reported to have done?
options: Denied breaking any rules
Closed the drain near the river
Published its own test results
questions.explanation: The sentence says the company is reported to have denied breaking any rules. The perfect infinitive refers to an earlier denial.

questions.question: What do the recent tests corroborate?
options: Earlier evidence of sediment
The identity of the construction firm
The exact source of the pollution
questions.explanation: The tests support earlier evidence of sediment, but they do not identify its exact source.

questions.question: What will the council do next?
options: Publish new results next month
Stop all road work immediately
Close the river throughout the summer
questions.explanation: The final sentence says the council has promised to publish new results next month.

questions.question: Why is the reason for the river's change still uncertain?
options: The evidence does not identify the exact source.
No samples have been collected.
The upstream readings were all abnormal.
questions.answer: The evidence does not identify the exact source.
questions.explanation: The passage says recent tests do not identify the exact source, so the cause has not been established.

questions.question: In the sentence The change is believed to stem from a combination of soil run-off and work on nearby roads, what does stem from mean?
options: Be caused by or originate in
Be measured beside
Be reported by
questions.answer: Be caused by or originate in
questions.explanation: Stem from introduces a likely origin or cause. Here, the report names soil run-off and road work as possible causes.

content.summary: Listen to two young journalists discussing editorial standards for an investigative piece. Pay attention to how passive reporting structures distance the writer from unverified claims and how weak forms function in rapid speech.
learningObjectives: Catch the main topic of an editorial conversation about investigative reporting.
Identify specific passive reporting structures used to establish journalistic distance.
Notice how auxiliary verbs and infinitives reduce to weak forms in fast spoken English.

keyPhrases.note: Used in journalistic reporting to state widespread claims without attributing them to a single speaker.
Indicates a probable origin or cause based on common understanding.
Combines a passive reporting verb with a perfect infinitive to report a past allegation.
A formal collocation describing institutional failure across an organization.

connectedSpeech.note: The alveolar plosive links smoothly across word boundaries into the vowel.
The infinitive particle reduces to a weak schwa sound in connected speech.
The auxiliary verb and preposition both reduce to schwas before the main verb.
Consonant to vowel linking connects the final plosive to the preposition.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Master Impersonal Reporting and Complex Passive Structures

content.summary: Journalists frequently use impersonal passive constructions to present claims, research findings, and widespread opinions without attributing them to a single source. Mastering these patterns allows you to maintain an objective tone while precisely indicating when an event occurred.

blueprintItems.title: Impersonal 'It' Construction
blueprintItems.formula: It + is/was + past participle of reporting verb + that + clause
blueprintItems.example: It is broadly asserted that remote working alters team dynamics.

blueprintItems.title: Personal Passive with Present Infinitive
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + is/are/was/were + past participle of reporting verb + to + base verb
blueprintItems.example: The phenomenon is believed to stem from shifts in consumer behavior.

blueprintItems.title: Personal Passive with Perfect Infinitive
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + is/are/was/were + past participle of reporting verb + to + have + past participle
blueprintItems.example: The suspect is reported to have fled the jurisdiction before daybreak.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use the perfect infinitive (to have + past participle) when the reported event occurred prior to the time of reporting.
mechanicsRules.badExample: The company is thought to lose significant revenue during the last quarter.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: The company is thought to have lost significant revenue during the last quarter.
mechanicsRules.why: The losses happened in the past relative to the present belief, requiring a perfect infinitive.

mechanicsRules.rule: Ensure the reporting verb agrees in number with the grammatical subject, not the noun inside the complement clause.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Several initiatives is reported to be under consideration by the board.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Several initiatives are reported to be under consideration by the board.
mechanicsRules.why: The subject 'initiatives' is plural, so the auxiliary verb must be 'are'.

mechanicsRules.rule: Do not attach dangling introductory participle phrases to an impersonal 'It' construction.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Examining the preliminary data, it is claimed that the trial was a success.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Based on the preliminary data, it is claimed that the trial was a success.
mechanicsRules.why: The pronoun 'it' cannot logically perform the action of examining data.

sampleSentences.en: It is broadly asserted that digital literacy plays a decisive role in modern employment.
sampleSentences.id: Ditegaskan secara luas bahwa literasi digital memainkan peran penting dalam dunia kerja modern.

sampleSentences.en: The economic downturn is believed to stem from persistent supply chain disruptions.
sampleSentences.id: Penurunan ekonomi diyakini berakar dari gangguan rantai pasok yang terus berlanjut.
sampleSentences.focus: Subject passive with present infinitive 'to stem'

sampleSentences.en: The former executive is understood to have concealed internal records from regulators.
sampleSentences.id: Mantan petinggi tersebut diketahui telah menyembunyikan catatan internal dari regulator.
sampleSentences.focus: Subject passive with perfect infinitive 'to have concealed'

sampleSentences.en: It was previously assumed that the policy had limited impact on inflation.
sampleSentences.id: Sebelumnya diasumsikan bahwa kebijakan tersebut memiliki dampak terbatas terhadap inflasi.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: it is broadly assert that remote work increases overall productivity
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: It is broadly asserted that remote work increases overall productivity.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Ditegaskan secara luas bahwa kerja jarak jauh meningkatkan produktivitas secara keseluruhan.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Capitalize the first word, use the past participle 'asserted' after 'is', and finish with a period.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: the prime minister is reported to left the summit early on friday
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: The prime minister is reported to have left the summit early on Friday.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Perdana menteri dilaporkan telah meninggalkan pertemuan puncak lebih awal pada hari Jumat.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Use a perfect infinitive ('to have left') for prior actions and capitalize proper nouns.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: several artifacts is believed to be preserved in the vault
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: Several artifacts are believed to be preserved in the vault.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Beberapa artefak diyakini disimpan di dalam brankas.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Use 'are' to agree with the plural subject 'artifacts' and capitalize sentence openings.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 1: Report on an Urban Transit Initiative
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write three to four sentences reporting on a city transportation initiative. Use at least one impersonal 'It is + past participle + that' structure and one 'Subject + is believed/expected to + base verb' structure.
guidedLabChallenges.example: It is broadly asserted that the planned light rail extension will reduce highway congestion. The project is expected to begin construction early next year. Commuters are understood to favor the revised route.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 2: Cover an Archaeological Finding
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write three to four sentences regarding an unexpected historical discovery. Use at least one personal passive structure with a perfect infinitive ('Subject + is thought/said to have + past participle') to refer to prior events.
guidedLabChallenges.example: The ancient fortress is believed to have stood intact until the thirteenth century. It is now claimed that early inhabitants built extensive drainage networks below the walls. Historians are expected to publish full excavation records next month.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence into an impersonal passive structure beginning with 'It is':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Many analysts assert that the housing market will stabilize by autumn.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'It is asserted that' followed by the original subordinate clause.
targetAnswers: It is asserted that the housing market will stabilize by autumn.
It is asserted by many analysts that the housing market will stabilize by autumn.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Active reporting clauses with 'analysts assert that...' become 'It is asserted that...' in impersonal journalistic prose.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence into a personal passive structure starting with the subject 'The rare species':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Scientists believe that the rare species lives primarily in coastal wetlands.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'is believed to' followed by the base verb 'live'.
targetAnswers: The rare species is believed to live primarily in coastal wetlands.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Because the action is present and ongoing, use the present infinitive: 'is believed to live'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence into a personal passive structure starting with 'The treasurer':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Inspectors suspect that the treasurer transferred funds to offshore accounts last year.
practicumQuestions.hint: The action took place in the past, so use 'to have transferred'.
targetAnswers: The treasurer is suspected to have transferred funds to offshore accounts last year.
practicumQuestions.explanation: When the reported action happened before the suspicion, employ the perfect infinitive: 'is suspected to have transferred'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the verb form error in this impersonal passive sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: It is broadly claim that renewable energy reduces long-term operational costs.
practicumQuestions.hint: Change 'claim' to its past participle form.
targetAnswers: It is broadly claimed that renewable energy reduces long-term operational costs.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The passive auxiliary 'is' must be followed by a past participle ('claimed'), not the base form.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Convert the impersonal 'It' construction into a personal passive starting with 'The proposed regulation':
practicumQuestions.promptText: It is expected that the proposed regulation will protect gig economy workers.
targetAnswers: The proposed regulation is expected to protect gig economy workers.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Moving the subject 'The proposed regulation' to the front converts the clause into 'is expected to protect'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Convert the sentence into a personal passive structure starting with 'The historic painting':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Experts think that the historic painting vanished during the Second World War.
practicumQuestions.hint: The loss occurred in the past, so use 'is thought to have vanished'.
targetAnswers: The historic painting is thought to have vanished during the Second World War.
practicumQuestions.explanation: A past action ('vanished') paired with a present belief ('experts think') requires the perfect infinitive 'to have vanished'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the subject-verb agreement error in the passive structure:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Both ministers is understood to have supported the controversial amendment.
targetAnswers: Both ministers are understood to have supported the controversial amendment.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Plural subjects require the plural auxiliary verb 'are'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the statements into one sentence using 'Although' and an impersonal passive structure ('it is acknowledged that'):
practicumQuestions.promptText: The factory creates jobs locally. Critics claim it increases carbon emissions.
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with 'Although it is acknowledged that...' and join the second clause.
targetAnswers: Although it is acknowledged that the factory creates jobs locally, critics claim it increases carbon emissions.
Although it is acknowledged that the factory creates jobs locally, it is claimed that it increases carbon emissions.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Combining clauses with 'Although' sets up a balanced contrast using formal impersonal phrasing.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the error in the infinitive construction:
practicumQuestions.promptText: The fugitive is reported to escaped across the northern border.
practicumQuestions.hint: Replace 'escaped' with the correct perfect infinitive formula: 'have' + past participle.
targetAnswers: The fugitive is reported to have escaped across the northern border.
practicumQuestions.explanation: A past infinitive construction requires 'to have' plus the past participle, not 'to' followed directly by a past tense verb.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Construct a complete journalistic sentence using the prompt words: 'The treaty / consider / be / significant milestone'.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use the present passive pattern: 'is considered to be'.
targetAnswers: The treaty is considered to be a significant milestone.
The treaty is considered to be a significant milestone in international diplomacy.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The standard personal passive structure here is 'Subject + is considered + to be + complement'.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Reporting Claims with Precision

content.summary: Practise reporting information without presenting an unverified claim as fact. Use structures such as “It is widely acknowledged that...” and “The cause is believed to stem from...” Speak clearly, place stress on the reporting verb and key information, and pause briefly between a claim and its supporting detail.
content.audioGuidance: Keep function words such as “is” and “to” short and connected to the words around them. Give the main stress to content words, especially reporting verbs and causes. Use a falling tone for a completed statement. Use a rising tone when checking information or inviting confirmation. Avoid sounding certain when describing an allegation that has not been proved.

pillars.name: Vowel Clarity
pillars.target: Distinguish short and long vowels in formal reporting vocabulary
pillars.explanation: Say the vowel in “allege” clearly and avoid reducing it so much that the word becomes difficult to recognise. Keep each syllable audible in “acknowledge” and “corroborate”.

pillars.name: Word Stress
pillars.target: Make the main syllable clear in longer vocabulary
pillars.explanation: Stress the second syllable of “assert” and “allege”. In “acknowledge”, make the first syllable prominent. Clear stress helps listeners identify the key reporting verb.

pillars.name: Sentence Stress
pillars.target: Emphasise the claim, source, and reported cause
pillars.explanation: In “The phenomenon is believed to stem from poor planning”, give the strongest stress to “phenomenon”, “believed”, “stem”, and “poor planning”. Keep auxiliary verbs lighter.

pillars.name: Measured Intonation
pillars.target: Use a calm, neutral tone for journalistic reporting
pillars.explanation: Use a steady falling tone for statements. Keep your voice neutral when reporting allegations, and do not let your intonation imply that an unproven accusation is confirmed.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Keep the main stress on the second syllable in both words.
The main stress stays on the second syllable when the noun form is used.
The first syllable carries the main stress in both forms.
Keep the strongest stress on “ROB” in both forms.

drills.targetText: It is broadly asserted that the new policy may reduce delays.
drills.phonetic: /ɪt ɪz ˈbrɔːdli əˈsɜːtɪd ðət ðə njuː ˈpɒləsi meɪ rɪˈdjuːs dɪˈleɪz/
drills.focus: Stress the reporting verb and the main claim
drills.hint: Keep “it is that” light, then make “asserted” and “reduce delays” clear.

drills.targetText: The company is alleged to have ignored repeated warnings.
drills.phonetic: /ðə ˈkʌmpəni ɪz əˈledʒd tə həv ɪɡˈnɔːd rɪˈpiːtɪd ˈwɔːnɪŋz/
drills.focus: Pronouncing an allegation carefully and neutrally
drills.hint: Do not stress “is” more than “alleged”. Keep your voice measured because the claim is not confirmed.

drills.targetText: The crisis is understood to stem from years of poor planning.
drills.phonetic: /ðə ˈkraɪsɪs ɪz ˌʌndəˈstʊd tə stem frəm jɪəz əv pɔː ˈplænɪŋ/
drills.focus: Linking the passive reporting structure to its stated cause
drills.hint: Connect “to stem” smoothly, and give the strongest stress to “crisis”, “stem”, and “poor planning”.

drills.targetText: The latest findings are reported to corroborate earlier research.
drills.phonetic: /ðə ˈleɪtɪst ˈfaɪndɪŋz ə rɪˈpɔːtɪd tə kəˈrɒbəreɪt ˈɜːliə rɪˈsɜːtʃ/
drills.hint: Say each syllable in “corroborate” and stress “ROB”. Finish the statement with a calm falling tone.

roleplay.context: You are speaking live with a local news editor about a report on pollution near a river. The editor asks you to describe the available claims and evidence without treating allegations as proven facts.

turns.speaker: News Editor
turns.text: What have local residents said about the company’s activity near the river?
turns.translation: Apa yang dikatakan warga setempat tentang kegiatan perusahaan di dekat sungai?

turns.speaker: Reporter
turns.text: The company is alleged to have released waste into the river, but that claim has not been proved.
turns.translation: Perusahaan itu diduga telah membuang limbah ke sungai, tetapi tuduhan tersebut belum terbukti.

turns.speaker: News Editor
turns.text: Do the latest findings support the residents’ account?
turns.translation: Apakah temuan terbaru mendukung keterangan warga?

turns.speaker: Reporter
turns.text: Some findings are reported to corroborate their account, while further tests are still under way.
turns.translation: Beberapa temuan dilaporkan menguatkan keterangan mereka, sementara pengujian lebih lanjut masih berlangsung.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 30 seconds as a reporter summarising a public issue. Use at least one impersonal passive reporting structure.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Describe a local public issue and explain what is currently known about its cause and effects.
storyPoints: Introduce the issue and explain who or what is affected.
Report one claim using “It is widely acknowledged that...” or “It is broadly asserted that...”.
Explain a possible cause using “The problem is believed to stem from...” and distinguish confirmed information from uncertainty.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: It is widely acknowledged that the river is polluted, and the problem is believed to stem from untreated waste.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪt ɪz ˈwaɪdli əkˈnɒlɪdʒd ðət ðə ˈrɪvə ɪz pəˈluːtɪd ænd ðə ˈprɒbləm ɪz bɪˈliːvd tə stem frəm ʌnˈtriːtɪd weɪst/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use a neutral journalistic tone, a clear passive reporting structure, and careful language for information that is not confirmed.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 30 seconds about a research finding and its significance. Use impersonal reporting language.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Tell listeners what a recent study has found and how its findings relate to earlier research.
storyPoints: State the general topic and what researchers examined.
Report a finding with “The study is reported to have found...” or a similar structure.
Explain whether the finding corroborates earlier research and mention any limits or unanswered questions.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The findings are reported to corroborate earlier research, although more evidence is needed.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə ˈfaɪndɪŋz ə rɪˈpɔːtɪd tə kəˈrɒbəreɪt ˈɜːliə rɪˈsɜːtʃ ɔːlˈðəʊ mɔː ˈevɪdəns ɪz ˈniːdɪd/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Organise your report in a clear sequence. Emphasise the reported finding, but avoid claiming that one study proves a wider conclusion.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take the reporter’s role in a live call. Respond to the editor with a cautious, impersonal report.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: The editor asks what residents claim happened near a factory. Answer in two or three sentences and make clear whether the claim has been verified.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: A news editor is preparing a report about residents’ claims that a factory discharged waste. No official investigation has reached a conclusion.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a reporter speaking to your news editor. Report the allegation accurately, avoid presenting it as fact, and use an impersonal reporting structure.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The factory is alleged to have discharged waste, but the claim has not been independently verified.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə ˈfæktəri ɪz əˈledʒd tə həv dɪsˈtʃɑːdʒd weɪst bət ðə kleɪm hæz nɒt bɪn ˌɪndɪˈpendəntli ˈverɪfaɪd/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Keep the allegation separate from established facts. Use a neutral tone and avoid language that implies guilt.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond as the reporter when the editor asks what may have caused a transport disruption.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: The editor asks what may explain a series of train delays. Give a cautious explanation and mention that further information is expected.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: A news editor is checking a report about delays on a regional rail network. Early information points to maintenance problems, but the operator has not published a full statement.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a transport reporter. Use “is believed to stem from” or a similar structure, and make clear that the explanation is based on early information.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The disruption is believed to stem from maintenance problems, although the operator has yet to confirm the cause.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə dɪsˈrʌpʃən ɪz bɪˈliːvd tə stem frəm ˈmeɪntənəns ˈprɒbləmz ɔːlˈðəʊ ði ˈɒpəreɪtə hæz jet tə kənˈfɜːm ðə kɔːz/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Present the proposed cause as a belief based on early information, not as a confirmed explanation.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Answer the editor’s question about how widely a public concern is recognised.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: The editor asks whether people agree that the local health service needs change. Give a balanced response using “It is widely acknowledged that...”
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are discussing a local health service report. Community groups have called for improvements, while officials say changes are already planned.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a reporter speaking with an editor. Explain what is broadly accepted and distinguish that from disagreement about the solution.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: It is widely acknowledged that the service needs improvement, although opinions differ on how it should be reformed.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪt ɪz ˈwaɪdli əkˈnɒlɪdʒd ðət ðə ˈsɜːvɪs niːdz ɪmˈpruːvmənt ɔːlˈðəʊ əˈpɪnjənz ˈdɪfə ɒn haʊ ɪt ʃʊd biː rɪˈfɔːmd/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use “acknowledged” for a broadly accepted point, then describe the disagreement without overstating consensus.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond to the editor’s question about new evidence in an ongoing investigation.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: The editor asks whether newly released documents support earlier reports. Explain what the documents appear to show and what remains uncertain.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: An editor is reviewing a public investigation. Newly released documents appear to support parts of earlier reporting, but the documents have not yet been assessed by an independent panel.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a reporter. Use “are reported to corroborate” or a similar structure, and mention the need for further review.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The documents are reported to corroborate earlier accounts, but their significance still needs independent review.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə ˈdɒkjʊmənts ə rɪˈpɔːtɪd tə kəˈrɒbəreɪt ˈɜːliə əˈkaʊnts bət ðeə sɪɡˈnɪfɪkəns stɪl niːdz ˌɪndɪˈpendənt rɪˈvjuː/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Make the reported support clear, but do not treat the documents as a final independent conclusion.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say one natural sentence for each word: “assert”, “allege”, “acknowledge”, “stem from”, “impersonal”, and “corroborate”. Use each word in a journalistic or research context.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Use “allege” for an unproved accusation and “corroborate” for evidence that supports an earlier claim.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The findings corroborate earlier research, while the separate allegation remains unproved.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə ˈfaɪndɪŋz kəˈrɒbəreɪt ˈɜːliə rɪˈsɜːtʃ waɪl ðə ˈsepərət ˌælɪˈɡeɪʃən rɪˈmeɪnz ʌnˈpruːvd/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Choose each word accurately. In particular, distinguish an allegation that is unproved from evidence that corroborates a claim.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Transform these direct statements into impersonal reporting structures: “Experts say the crisis began with poor planning” and “Researchers believe the change will affect coastal towns.”
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Use “It is said that...” or “The crisis is believed to...” and keep the reported meaning clear.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The crisis is believed to have stemmed from poor planning, and coastal towns are expected to be affected.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə ˈkraɪsɪs ɪz bɪˈliːvd tə həv stemd frəm pɔː ˈplænɪŋ ænd ˈkəʊstl taʊnz ə ɪkˈspektɪd tə biː əˈfektɪd/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use a suitable passive reporting verb and the correct infinitive form. Use a perfect infinitive for a cause that began in the past.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say “assert”, “allege”, “acknowledge”, and “corroborate” twice. Make the main stressed syllable prominent in each word.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Listen for the strong syllables: as-SERT, al-LEGE, ac-KNOWL-edge, cor-ROB-o-rate.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: It is broadly asserted that the evidence may corroborate the report.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪt ɪz ˈbrɔːdli əˈsɜːtɪd ðət ði ˈevɪdəns meɪ kəˈrɒbəreɪt ðə rɪˈpɔːt/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Make the stressed syllable clear without exaggerating every syllable. The main stress falls on the second syllable in “assert”, “allege”, and “corroborate”, and on the first syllable in “acknowledge”.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Read the statement with a falling tone, then read the confirmation question with a rising tone.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Statement: “The cause is believed to stem from poor planning.” Question: “Is that explanation confirmed?”
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The cause is believed to stem from poor planning. Is that explanation confirmed?
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə kɔːz ɪz bɪˈliːvd tə stem frəm pɔː ˈplænɪŋ | ɪz ðæt ˌekspləˈneɪʃən kənˈfɜːmd/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Let your voice fall at the end of the complete statement. Let it rise on the confirmation question, while keeping the overall delivery calm and neutral.
